category: Chemical Species Transport (Chemical Reaction Engineering Module)
description: Species transport interfaces of the Chemical Reaction Engineering Module (diluted and concentrated species in free, porous, catalytic, packed-bed, fracture and vapor settings) and their domain and boundary features. Type strings in the Java examples were taken from the COMSOL 6.4 Application Library models.

tools.name: Transport of Diluted Species in Porous Media (tds)
tools.description: Variant of the Transport of Diluted Species interface with the Mass transport in porous media option selected and a Porous Medium node added by default. It models solutes carried by a fluid that fully (saturated) or partially (unsaturated) fills a porous matrix, including diffusion with effective diffusivities, convection, migration, dispersion, adsorption and volatilization. Use it for chromatography columns, monolith catalysts, soils, filters and battery or fuel-cell electrode pores.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Chemical Species Transport > Transport of Diluted Species in Porous Media; Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("tds", "DilutedSpeciesInPorousMedia", "geom1")

parameters.name: prop("TransportMechanism") Convection / Migration
parameters.description: Enable convective transport (default on) and migration of ions in an electric field.

parameters.name: MassTransferInPorousMedia
parameters.description: On by default; activates Porous Medium, Unsaturated Porous Medium, Packed Bed, Porous Catalyst, Volatilization, Species Source and Porous Electrode Coupling.

parameters.name: DispersionInPorousMedia / VolatilizationInPartiallySaturatedPorousMedia
parameters.description: Transport-mechanism switches that make the Dispersion and Volatilization features available.

parameters.name: Porous Medium > Fluid / Porous Matrix
parameters.description: Default subnodes defining fluid diffusivity, velocity field, porosity and effective diffusivity model (Millington-Quirk, Bruggeman, tortuosity).

tools.notes: Same interface as Transport of Diluted Species (tag tds) with other defaults; the Transport of Diluted Species in Packed Beds entry also builds on the DilutedSpeciesInPorousMedia type. Porous transport requires the Chemical Reaction Engineering, Battery Design, Fuel Cell & Electrolyzer, Porous Media Flow or Subsurface Flow Module.

tools.name: Transport of Diluted Species in Porous Catalysts (tds)
tools.description: Transport of Diluted Species interface with a Porous Catalyst node added by default, found under the Reacting Flow in Porous Media group. It studies adsorption/desorption of bulk species on the fluid-solid interface and heterogeneous reactions between bulk and surface species, using a linear driving force model with a lumped mass transfer coefficient. Volumetric reactions in the pores can be added under the Fluid subnode.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Chemical Species Transport > Reacting Flow in Porous Media > Transport of Diluted Species in Porous Catalysts; Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("tds", "DilutedSpeciesInPorousCatalysts", "geom1")

parameters.name: Porous Catalyst
parameters.description: Default domain node with Fluid and Porous Matrix subnodes; defines specific surface area Sarea, surface species and site densities.

parameters.name: Adsorption (Porous Catalyst)
parameters.description: Subnode for adsorption isotherms/kinetics of bulk species onto the catalyst surface.

parameters.name: Surface Reaction (Porous Catalyst)
parameters.description: Subnode for heterogeneous reaction rates of bulk, adsorbed and surface species.

tools.notes: Couple surface chemistry from a Chemistry interface (surface species appear as chem.R_X_surf rates). Requires the Chemical Reaction Engineering Module.

tools.name: Transport of Diluted Species in Packed Beds (tds)
tools.description: Transport of Diluted Species interface with a Packed Bed node added by default for reactors filled with porous catalyst pellets. The bimodal porosity is resolved: bulk transport in the interparticle voids plus intraparticle diffusion and reaction inside pellets described in an extra radial dimension at every point of the bed. Several pellet types can be combined through Pellets subnodes of a Porous Material.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Chemical Species Transport > Reacting Flow in Porous Media > Transport of Diluted Species in Packed Beds; Packed Bed node Java type: "PackedBed"

parameters.name: Packed Bed: BedReactorType
parameters.description: PackedBed or moving packed bed; bed porosity poro and bed velocity umb.

parameters.name: Pellets (PorousPellet)
parameters.description: Pellet type (Catalyst or Shrinking Core), pellet porosity, radius/size distribution, surface species.

parameters.name: Pellet-Fluid Interface
parameters.description: Continuous concentration or film resistance (mass flux) coupling with Sherwood correlations.

tools.notes: The Packed Bed node needs a Porous Material with Pellets subnodes on the bed domains. Pair with Heat Transfer in Packed Beds and a Reacting Flow in Porous Media coupling for nonisothermal reactors.

tools.name: Transport of Diluted Species in Moving Packed Beds / Shrinking Core (tds)
tools.description: Variants of the packed-bed interface where the pellet bed moves relative to the reactor (Bed Type set to Moving packed bed), adding the bed velocity convection term for intraparticle species. Setting the Pellet Type to Shrinking Core model switches to reactant pellets whose solid core is consumed from the outside inward, leaving a porous product layer. Used for moving-bed reactors, gas-solid reactions, roasting and reduction of ores.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Chemical Species Transport > Reacting Flow in Porous Media > Moving Packed Bed > Transport of Diluted Species in Moving Packed Beds (or ..., Shrinking Core)

parameters.name: Bed Type
parameters.description: Packed bed or Moving packed bed (on the Packed Bed node); moving beds need Bed Inlet and Bed Outlet boundaries.

parameters.name: Pellet Type
parameters.description: Porous catalyst or Shrinking Core model (on Pellets).

parameters.name: Shrinking Core Reactions / Porous Layer Reactions
parameters.description: Core-surface reactions and reactions in the reacted porous layer.

tools.example:
1. Add Transport of Diluted Species in Packed Beds and a Porous Material with a Pellets subnode.
2. On Packed Bed set Bed Type = Moving packed bed and the bed velocity.
3. On Pellets set Pellet Type = Shrinking Core model; add Shrinking Core Reactions with the solid-species rate.
4. Add Bed Inlet (pellet inlet concentrations, initial core radius factor rc0f) and Bed Outlet.
tools.notes: The Transport of Diluted Species in Packed Beds, Shrinking Core variant (fixed bed) also exists. Requires the Chemical Reaction Engineering Module.

tools.name: Transport of Diluted Species in Fractures (dsf)
tools.description: Boundary-level interface for solute transport along thin porous fractures, including diffusion, dispersion, convection and chemical reactions, with the fracture thickness as a parameter instead of meshed geometry. It works on boundaries in 2D, 2D axisymmetric and 3D, solving for the molar concentration of each species. The same physics is also available as the Fracture node in the porous-media transport interfaces.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Chemical Species Transport > Transport of Diluted Species in Fractures (default name dsf)

parameters.name: Convection
parameters.description: Additional transport mechanism checkbox on the interface.

parameters.name: Fracture thickness dfr
parameters.description: Defined on the Fluid/Fracture Material nodes; porosity epsilon_p of the fracture.

parameters.name: Adsorption / Dispersion / Reactions / Species Source
parameters.description: Boundary features equivalent to the domain features of TDS in porous media.

parameters.name: Consistent stabilization
parameters.description: Streamline and crosswind diffusion (Do Carmo and Galeao or Codina).

tools.example:
1. Add Darcy's Law with a Fracture Flow node for the fracture velocity.
2. Add Transport of Diluted Species in Fractures on the fracture boundaries.
3. Set Fluid > velocity from Darcy's Law, diffusion coefficient and Fracture Material thickness.
4. Add Inflow on the upstream edge and Outflow downstream, then run a Time Dependent study.
tools.notes: Available only in some add-on products (Chemical Reaction Engineering, Subsurface Flow, Porous Media Flow). The Java type string is not given in the local documentation.

tools.name: Transport of Concentrated Species in Porous Media (tcs)
tools.description: Transport of Concentrated Species interface with a Porous Medium node added by default, solving for mass fractions of all species in a fluid mixture flowing through a porous matrix. Convection, multicomponent diffusion (Maxwell-Stefan, mixture-averaged, Fick) and migration are available, and regions of free flow can be combined with porous regions. Used for gas-phase catalytic beds, pyrolysis, hydrogen storage and SOFC/SOEC electrode gas transport.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Chemical Species Transport > Transport of Concentrated Species in Porous Media; Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("tcs", "ConcentratedSpeciesInPorousMedia", "geom1")

parameters.name: prop("TransportMechanism") DiffusionModel
parameters.description: MaxwellStefan, MixtureAveraged or FicksLaw.

parameters.name: prop("SpeciesProperties") FromMassConstraint
parameters.description: Index of the species computed from the mass constraint (choose the most abundant one).

parameters.name: Porous Medium > Fluid / Porous Matrix
parameters.description: Fluid density/velocity/diffusivities and porosity with effective diffusivity model.

tools.notes: Couple velocity and density through a Reacting Flow in Porous Media multiphysics node to include Stefan velocity and mass sources in the flow.

tools.name: Transport of Concentrated Species in Porous Catalysts / Packed Beds (tcs)
tools.description: Concentrated-mixture counterparts of the diluted porous-catalyst and packed-bed interfaces. The Porous Catalysts variant adds a Porous Catalyst node for adsorption, desorption and heterogeneous reactions with surface species; the Packed Beds variant adds a Packed Bed node resolving pellets in an extra dimension, including intraparticle flow velocity, pressure and pellet temperature. Use them when no solvent dominates, for example gas-phase catalytic reforming.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Chemical Species Transport > Reacting Flow in Porous Media > Transport of Concentrated Species in Porous Catalysts / in Packed Beds

parameters.name: Porous Catalyst / Packed Bed
parameters.description: Default main node; Fluid, Porous Matrix or Pellets subnodes define phase properties.

parameters.name: Pellet Temperature
parameters.description: From fluid or from a Heat Transfer in Pellets interface (packed beds).

parameters.name: Surface Species
parameters.description: Table of surface species solved for on the catalyst.

tools.example:
1. Add Transport of Concentrated Species in Packed Beds and a Porous Material with Pellets.
2. Select the Maxwell-Stefan or mixture-averaged diffusion model.
3. Add a Chemistry interface with Define variables for porous pellets to supply intraparticle rates.
4. Couple Free and Porous Media Flow with the Reacting Flow in Porous Media coupling.
tools.notes: Requires the Chemical Reaction Engineering Module. Java type strings for these entries are not listed in the local documentation.

tools.name: Transport of Concentrated Species in Vapor (tcs)
tools.description: Transport of Concentrated Species interface specialised for vapor mixtures in contact with liquids, adding the Vapor Inflow, Vapor-Liquid Interface and Vapor-Liquid-Solution Interface features. The vapor pressure at the interface is computed from liquid composition, temperature and pressure (for example from a Thermodynamics package), giving evaporation or condensation fluxes and latent heat. Used for droplet evaporation, distillation and humidifiers.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Chemical Species Transport > Transport of Concentrated Species in Vapor; Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("tcs", "ConcentratedSpeciesInVapor", "geom1")

parameters.name: DiffusionModel
parameters.description: Mixture-averaged by default; Maxwell-Stefan or Fick's law also available.

parameters.name: Vapor-Liquid Interface
parameters.description: Exterior boundary evaporation condition with vapor pressure model (Thermodynamics or user-defined).

parameters.name: Vapor-Liquid-Solution Interface
parameters.description: Interior boundary condition for multicomponent liquids solved in an adjacent domain.

tools.notes: The Vapor-Liquid Equilibrium multiphysics interfaces combine this interface with laminar or turbulent flow and heat transfer.

tools.name: Diffusion Model: Maxwell-Stefan / Mixture-Averaged / Fick's Law (Transport of Concentrated Species)
tools.description: Interface-level choice of the multicomponent diffusion formulation in Transport of Concentrated Species. Maxwell-Stefan is the most detailed and most expensive and needs binary Maxwell-Stefan diffusivities of all pairs; Mixture-averaged uses a diffusion coefficient of each species into the mixture, is cheaper, more robust and stabilised; Fick's law is a robust low-order model for Fickian diffusion or when multicomponent diffusivities are unknown. Thermal diffusion and migration terms can be added to the flux.
tools.usage: Transport of Concentrated Species > Transport Mechanisms > Diffusion model; Java: model.component("comp1").physics("tcs").prop("TransportMechanism").set("DiffusionModel", "MaxwellStefan")

parameters.name: DiffusionModel
parameters.description: MaxwellStefan | MixtureAveraged | FicksLaw.

parameters.name: Fluid > Dik
parameters.description: Binary Maxwell-Stefan diffusivities (from material, Chemistry or user input) or Fickian diffusivities.

parameters.name: AdvancedSettings: MixtureDiffusionCorrection, DiffusionFluxType
parameters.description: Mixture diffusion correction and whether the flux uses mole-fraction or mass-fraction gradients.

parameters.name: Regularization
parameters.description: Regularization of reaction rate expressions near zero mass fraction.

tools.notes: Maxwell-Stefan is intended for diffusion-dominated problems; for convection-dominated reacting flow the mixture-averaged model is usually preferred. Diffusivities can be computed automatically by a Chemistry interface with Calculate transport properties.

tools.name: Transport Mechanisms Settings (Transport of Diluted Species)
tools.description: Interface-level section of Transport of Diluted Species that decides which terms enter the mass balance: diffusion is always included, while convection, migration in electric field, mass transport in porous media, dispersion and volatilization are switched on by checkboxes. The section also governs stabilization (streamline and crosswind diffusion) and the conservative or nonconservative material balance form. Choosing the mechanisms first determines which domain and boundary features appear.
tools.usage: Transport of Diluted Species > Transport Mechanisms; Java: model.component("comp1").physics("tds").prop("TransportMechanism").set("Migration", "1")

parameters.name: Convection
parameters.description: Default on; requires a velocity field on the Fluid node.

parameters.name: Migration
parameters.description: Nernst-Einstein or user mobility; needs charges on Species Properties and an electric potential.

parameters.name: MassTransferInPorousMedia
parameters.description: Enables porous-media features.

parameters.name: prop("AdvancedSettings") ConvectiveTerm
parameters.description: noncons (default) or cons; use conservative form for compressible flow.

parameters.name: Compute boundary fluxes
parameters.description: Adds accurate flux variables ndflux_c and ntflux_c.

tools.notes: Migration and porous-media transport are only available with certain add-on modules. Crosswind diffusion makes the equation system nonlinear.

tools.name: Fluid (Transport of Diluted Species)
tools.description: Default domain node holding the transport equations and material properties of Transport of Diluted Species. It takes the temperature model input, the solvent velocity field (user-defined or from a fluid flow interface), and the diffusion coefficient of every species (isotropic, diagonal, symmetric or full tensor) from a material, a Chemistry interface or user input. With migration enabled it also defines mobilities and the electric potential.
tools.usage: Physics > Transport of Diluted Species > Fluid (cdm1); Java type: "Fluid"

parameters.name: u
parameters.description: Velocity field components (user defined or model input from Laminar Flow etc.).

parameters.name: D_c
parameters.description: Fluid diffusion coefficient tensor of species c; DiffusionCoefficientSource = mat, chem or user defined.

parameters.name: MobilityModel / um
parameters.description: Nernst-Einstein relation or user mobility when migration is active.

parameters.name: V
parameters.description: Electric potential for migration.

tools.notes: In porous interfaces the same settings are on the Fluid subnode of Porous Medium, with effective diffusivity corrections from the Porous Matrix.

tools.name: Species Properties / Species Charges (Transport of Diluted Species)
tools.description: Node that defines per-species parameters when Migration in electric field is enabled: the charge number z of each species and, when a nonideal Species Activity model (Debye-Hueckel or user defined) is chosen, the ion size or activity coefficient. It is labelled Species Charges when only charges are available. Required for electrophoresis, electroosmosis and Nernst-Planck type transport.
tools.usage: Physics > Transport of Diluted Species > Species Properties (sp1); Java type: "SpeciesProperties"

parameters.name: z_c
parameters.description: Charge number of each species (signed, dimensionless).

parameters.name: a0
parameters.description: Ion size number for the Debye-Hueckel activity model.

parameters.name: f
parameters.description: User-defined activity coefficient.

tools.notes: The Species activity model itself is chosen on the interface level (prop SpeciesActivity = Ideal, DebyeHuckel or UserDefined).

tools.name: Mass-Based Concentrations (Transport of Diluted Species)
tools.description: Adds postprocessing variables for mass-based concentrations (kg/m^3) and mass fractions of all species in a Transport of Diluted Species model. It needs the solvent density (from material or user defined) and the molar mass of each species. It does not change the solved equations.
tools.usage: Physics > Transport of Diluted Species > Mass-Based Concentrations (domain node)

parameters.name: rho_solvent
parameters.description: Solvent density, From material or User defined.

parameters.name: M_c
parameters.description: Molar mass of each species.

tools.example:
1. Right-click Transport of Diluted Species > Mass-Based Concentrations.
2. Enter molar masses, e.g. 0.058[kg/mol] for NaCl.
3. Plot the generated mass fraction variables in a Surface plot.
tools.notes: Useful when reporting ppm or wt% while keeping the molar formulation.

tools.name: Reactions (Transport of Diluted Species)
tools.description: Domain node that adds volumetric reaction rates R_i (mol/(m^3*s)) to the species balances. Rates can be user-defined expressions or taken automatically from a coupled Chemistry interface through its species matching table. In porous media the reacting volume (pore volume or total volume) and the reaction heat source can also be specified.
tools.usage: Physics > Transport of Diluted Species > Reactions (reac1); Java type: "Reactions"

parameters.name: Chemistry / chemTag
parameters.description: Coupled Chemistry interface, or User defined.

parameters.name: R_<c>
parameters.description: Rate expression for each species, e.g. R_cA = -k*cA*cB.

parameters.name: ReactingVolumeType
parameters.description: PoreVolume or TotalVolume (porous media).

parameters.name: ReactionHeatSource / Q
parameters.description: Heat of reaction taken from Chemistry or user-defined.

tools.notes: For fast reversible reactions use Equilibrium Reaction instead of stiff kinetics.

tools.name: Inflow (Transport of Diluted Species)
tools.description: Specifies the concentration of all species at an inlet boundary. The Concentration constraint option imposes the values pointwise, while Flux (Danckwerts) prescribes the total inflow flux from an upstream concentration and the local velocity, which is more robust when fast reactions occur near the inlet. For a subset of species use the Concentration node instead.
tools.usage: Physics > Transport of Diluted Species > Inflow (in1); Java type: "Inflow"

parameters.name: c0
parameters.description: Inlet (or upstream) concentration of each species.

parameters.name: BoundaryConditionType
parameters.description: ConcentrationConstraint or FluxDanckwerts.

parameters.name: constraintType
parameters.description: Constraint settings (advanced physics options).

tools.notes: Available in Electroanalysis when convection is enabled. Equilibrium Reaction can modify inflow values to satisfy equilibrium.

tools.name: Outflow (Transport of Diluted Species)
tools.description: Outlet condition assuming that convection (and migration for ions) dominates the transport across the boundary so that the diffusive flux normal to it is zero. Species leave the domain with the fluid. It requires the Convection or Migration mechanism to be active.
tools.usage: Physics > Transport of Diluted Species > Outflow (out1); Java type: "Outflow"

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Outlet boundaries; no further inputs.

tools.notes: Where backflow may occur use Open Boundary. Application example: Chemical_Reaction_Engineering_Module/Reactors_with_Mass_Transfer/boat_reactor.

tools.name: Flux (Transport of Diluted Species)
tools.description: Prescribes the inward molar flux of selected species across a boundary, for example from reactions, phase change or exchange with an unmodelled surrounding. By default the diffusive plus migrative flux is prescribed; convection can be included, and the External convection type uses a mass transfer coefficient kc and bulk concentration cb.
tools.usage: Physics > Transport of Diluted Species > Flux (fl1); Java type: "FluxBoundary"

parameters.name: species / J0
parameters.description: Checkbox per species and inward flux value (negative for outward).

parameters.name: FluxType
parameters.description: GeneralInwardFlux or ExternalConvection (kc*(cb-c)).

parameters.name: IncludeConvection
parameters.description: Include the convective flux in the prescribed total flux.

parameters.name: kc, cb
parameters.description: Mass transfer coefficient and bulk concentration for external convection.

tools.notes: See Prescribing Conditions on Fluid-Solid Interfaces when the boundary separates phases.

tools.name: Flux Discontinuity (Transport of Diluted Species)
tools.description: Interior-boundary condition that imposes a jump N0 in the total species flux across the boundary. It represents a surface source or sink such as a surface reaction, adsorption or desorption located on an internal wall or membrane. Each species can be activated individually.
tools.usage: Physics > Transport of Diluted Species > Flux Discontinuity (interior boundaries)

parameters.name: N0
parameters.description: Jump in total flux (mol/(m^2*s)) for each selected species.

tools.example:
1. Draw an interior boundary representing a reactive membrane.
2. Add Flux Discontinuity on it and enter N0 = k_s*c for the produced species.
3. Solve with a Stationary study and plot tds.tflux_c.
tools.notes: Use Thin Diffusion Barrier or Partition Condition when the membrane resistance or concentration jump matters.

tools.name: Open Boundary (Transport of Diluted Species)
tools.description: Boundary condition for boundaries where fluid can both enter and leave. Where the flow enters, the exterior concentration is prescribed; where it leaves, an outflow-type condition is applied. The flow direction usually comes from a fluid flow interface via the velocity model input.
tools.usage: Physics > Transport of Diluted Species > Open Boundary

parameters.name: c0
parameters.description: Exterior concentration of each species.

tools.example:
1. Couple Laminar Flow (with an Open Boundary) to Transport of Diluted Species.
2. Add Open Boundary to the same boundary and set the exterior concentration to the ambient value.
3. Solve the flow first, then the transport.
tools.notes: Available only in a limited set of add-on products.

tools.name: Thin Impermeable Barrier (Transport of Diluted Species)
tools.description: Interior-boundary feature that models a thin mass-transfer barrier without meshing it: a no-flux condition is applied on each side, allowing a concentration discontinuity across the boundary. Combine it with an Interior Wall in the flow interface to model a thin solid wall in coupled flow and transport.
tools.usage: Physics > Transport of Diluted Species > Thin Impermeable Barrier (tib1); Java type: "ThinImpermeableBarrier"

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Interior boundaries acting as barriers.

tools.notes: For a permeable membrane use Thin Diffusion Barrier.

tools.name: Line Mass Source / Point Mass Source (Transport of Diluted Species)
tools.description: Singular species sources: Line Mass Source injects or removes species along an edge (3D) or at a point (2D, representing a line out of plane) with strength in mol/(m*s); Point Mass Source does the same from a point in mol/s. Positive values inject species and negative values remove them. Sources on a symmetry plane act with twice the given physical strength.
tools.usage: Physics > Transport of Diluted Species > Line Mass Source (lms1) / Point Mass Source (pms1); Java types: "MassSourceLine", "MassSourcePoint"

parameters.name: qs
parameters.description: Source strength per species (mol/(m*s) for lines, mol/s for points).

tools.notes: Available in selected add-on products. Point sources give mesh-dependent local values; evaluate integrated quantities instead.

tools.name: Equilibrium Reaction (Transport of Diluted Species)
tools.description: Domain node for a reaction so fast that equilibrium holds everywhere at all times; the equilibrium rate Req is solved as an extra degree of freedom that enforces the equilibrium condition. The definition can be picked from an equilibrium reaction of a coupled Chemistry interface or entered via equilibrium constant, stoichiometric coefficients and unit activity concentration. Optionally inflow concentrations are adjusted to satisfy equilibrium.
tools.usage: Physics > Transport of Diluted Species > Equilibrium Reaction (requires two or more species)

parameters.name: Chemistry / Equilibrium reaction formula
parameters.description: Pick a coupled equilibrium reaction, or None for manual definition.

parameters.name: Equilibrium definition
parameters.description: Equilibrium constant Keq or User defined equilibrium expression.

parameters.name: Stoichiometric coefficients
parameters.description: Per species for the manual definition.

parameters.name: Apply equilibrium condition on inflow boundaries
parameters.description: Corrects inflow concentrations.

tools.example:
1. Add Equilibrium Reaction to TDS for HA <=> H+ + A-.
2. Enter Keq = Ka and stoichiometric coefficients -1, 1, 1.
3. Keep kinetic reactions in a separate Reactions node and solve.
tools.notes: Available with the Chemical Reaction Engineering and electrochemistry modules. Surface Equilibrium Reaction is the boundary analogue.

tools.name: Surface Reactions (Transport of Diluted Species)
tools.description: Boundary node that sets the species boundary flux equal to the rate of heterogeneous reactions at a surface. Rates J0 per species can be typed in or picked from a Chemistry interface that defines surface reactions. Used for chemical vapor deposition, catalytic walls and electrodes without electrochemistry.
tools.usage: Physics > Transport of Diluted Species > Surface Reactions (srf1); Java type: "SurfaceReactionsFlux"

parameters.name: J0_<c>
parameters.description: Surface reaction rate (mol/(m^2*s)) of each species.

tools.notes: To track surface species coverage use the Surface Reactions (sr) interface together with this node.

tools.name: Surface Equilibrium Reaction (Transport of Diluted Species)
tools.description: Boundary counterpart of Equilibrium Reaction that enforces an equilibrium condition for a reaction on a surface, solving for the reaction rate as an extra boundary degree of freedom. Settings mirror the domain Equilibrium Reaction (from Chemistry or manual equilibrium constant). Requires at least two species.
tools.usage: Physics > Transport of Diluted Species > Surface Equilibrium Reaction (seqreac1); Java type: "SurfaceEquilibriumReaction"

parameters.name: Equilibrium constant / expression
parameters.description: Keq or user-defined equilibrium condition.

parameters.name: Stoichiometric coefficients
parameters.description: Of the participating species.

tools.notes: Available in a limited set of add-on products.

tools.name: Fast Irreversible Surface Reaction (Transport of Diluted Species)
tools.description: Boundary node for an irreversible surface reaction limited only by mass transport of a reactant to the surface. It sets the rate-limiting species concentration to zero at the boundary and balances the fluxes of the other participating species (and current densities) using the stoichiometric coefficients. Useful for diffusion-limited electrodes or catalytic walls.
tools.usage: Physics > Transport of Diluted Species > Fast Irreversible Surface Reaction

parameters.name: Rate limiting species
parameters.description: Species whose concentration is set to zero.

parameters.name: Stoichiometric Coefficients
parameters.description: For all species in the reaction.

tools.example:
1. Add Fast Irreversible Surface Reaction on a catalytic wall.
2. Choose O2 as rate limiting species with coefficient -1 and product CO2 with +1.
3. Solve and integrate tds.ntflux to get the limiting reaction rate.
tools.notes: Available in a limited set of add-on products.

tools.name: Porous Electrode Coupling (Transport of Diluted Species)
tools.description: Domain node that adds molar sources coupled to one or more Porous Electrode Reaction nodes of an electrochemistry interface. The sources follow Faraday's law from the number of electrons, stoichiometric coefficients and volumetric current densities given in Reaction Coefficients subnodes. In Transport of Concentrated Species the molar sources are multiplied by molar masses.
tools.usage: Physics > Transport of Diluted Species > Porous Electrode Coupling (pec1) > Reaction Coefficients (rc1); Java type: "PorousElectrodeCoupling"

parameters.name: Reaction Coefficients subnodes
parameters.description: One per coupled porous electrode reaction (iv, nm, Vi).

tools.notes: For gas diffusion electrodes with significant net mass sources also add the corresponding mass source in the flow interface (a Reacting Flow coupling does this automatically). Electrode Surface Coupling is the boundary analogue.

tools.name: Reaction Coefficients (Electrode Surface / Porous Electrode Coupling)
tools.description: Subnode of Electrode Surface Coupling and Porous Electrode Coupling that converts an electrode current density into species fluxes or sources via Faraday's law. The coupled reaction can be any Electrode Reaction (iloc, A/m^2) or Porous Electrode Reaction (iv, A/m^3) in the model, or a user expression. Add one subnode per coupled reaction.
tools.usage: Physics > Transport of Diluted Species > Porous Electrode Coupling > Reaction Coefficients (rc1); Java type: "ReactionCoefficients"

parameters.name: iv_src / iv
parameters.description: Coupled volumetric (or surface iloc) current density, e.g. root.comp1.liion.pce1.per1.iv, or a user expression.

parameters.name: nm
parameters.description: Number of participating electrons.

parameters.name: Vi
parameters.description: Stoichiometric coefficient of each species (negative for reduced species in a reduction written as ox + ne- -> red).

tools.notes: Sign convention: the flux is -nu*i/(n*F); check the Electrode Reaction stoichiometry section for consistency.

tools.name: Adsorption (Transport of Diluted Species in Porous Media)
tools.description: Subnode of Porous Medium and Unsaturated Porous Medium that models sorption of solutes onto the porous matrix. The sorbed amount follows an isotherm (Langmuir, Freundlich, Toth, BET or user defined) and requires the dry bulk density or solid-phase density of the matrix. It introduces retardation of the concentration front.
tools.usage: Physics > Transport of Diluted Species in Porous Media > Porous Medium > Adsorption (ads1); Java type: "Adsorptions"

parameters.name: densityType / rho_db / rho_sp
parameters.description: Dry bulk density or solid phase density of the matrix.

parameters.name: SorptionType
parameters.description: Langmuir, Freundlich, Toth, BET or UserDefined.

parameters.name: KL, cPmax
parameters.description: Langmuir constant and adsorption maximum per species.

parameters.name: KF, NF, cref
parameters.description: Freundlich constant, exponent and reference concentration.

tools.notes: For adsorption on catalyst surfaces with surface reactions use the Porous Catalyst node.

tools.name: Dispersion (Transport of Diluted Species in Porous Media)
tools.description: Subnode of Porous Medium or Unsaturated Porous Medium adding mechanical dispersion caused by velocity variations around solid grains. The dispersion tensor is given by longitudinal and transverse dispersivities (isotropic or transverse isotropic media) or entered directly, optionally per species. It needs both porous-media transport and convection enabled.
tools.usage: Physics > Transport of Diluted Species in Porous Media > Porous Medium > Dispersion

parameters.name: Dispersion tensor
parameters.description: Dispersivity or User defined.

parameters.name: Dispersivity model
parameters.description: Isotropic (alpha_L, alpha_T) or Transverse isotropic (longitudinal, horizontal and vertical transverse).

parameters.name: Specify dispersion for each species individually
parameters.description: Per-species dispersion tensors.

tools.example:
1. Enable DispersionInPorousMedia on the interface.
2. Add Dispersion under Porous Medium and set alpha_L = 0.1[m], alpha_T = 0.01[m].
3. Run a Time Dependent study for a tracer plume.
tools.notes: Dispersion usually dominates molecular diffusion in groundwater and packed columns at moderate Peclet numbers.

tools.name: Unsaturated Porous Medium (Transport of Diluted Species in Porous Media)
tools.description: Domain node for solutes carried by a liquid that only partly fills the pores, with immobile gas pockets in the remaining pore space. Liquid, Gas and Porous Matrix subnodes define each phase, and adsorption, dispersion and volatilization of species into the gas phase can be included. Used for vadose-zone and soil contaminant transport.
tools.usage: Physics > Transport of Diluted Species in Porous Media > Unsaturated Porous Medium (with Liquid, Gas, Porous Matrix subnodes)

parameters.name: Liquid
parameters.description: Saturation or liquid volume fraction, velocity field and liquid diffusivities.

parameters.name: Gas
parameters.description: Gas diffusivities and volatilization (Henry) coefficients.

parameters.name: Porous Matrix
parameters.description: Porosity and effective diffusivity model.

tools.example:
1. Solve Richards' Equation for saturation and Darcy velocity.
2. Add Unsaturated Porous Medium in TDS in Porous Media and take liquid volume fraction and velocity from Richards' Equation.
3. Add Adsorption and Volatilization and run a transient study.
tools.notes: Only available in some add-on products (Subsurface Flow, Porous Media Flow, Chemical Reaction Engineering).

tools.name: Volatilization (Transport of Diluted Species in Porous Media)
tools.description: Boundary condition for mass transfer out of a partially saturated porous medium by volatilization: dissolved species vaporize at the boundary and are carried away into the surroundings. The flux is governed by a mass transfer coefficient hc, the volatilization coefficient kG from the adjacent Unsaturated Porous Medium, and the atmospheric concentration.
tools.usage: Physics > Transport of Diluted Species in Porous Media > Volatilization (boundary)

parameters.name: hc
parameters.description: Mass transfer coefficient, e.g. D_G/d_s for a stagnant diffusion layer.

parameters.name: cGatm
parameters.description: Species concentration in the surrounding atmosphere.

tools.example:
1. Enable VolatilizationInPartiallySaturatedPorousMedia on the interface.
2. Add Volatilization on the soil surface with hc = 1e-3[m/s] and cGatm = 0.
3. Compare volatilized mass with Mass Integration over time.
tools.notes: Requires the porous-media transport option and an Unsaturated Porous Medium domain.

tools.name: Species Source (Transport of Diluted Species in Porous Media)
tools.description: Domain node that adds source terms S_i (mol/(m^3*s)) to the species balances in porous domains, representing production or consumption not described by a Reactions node. Several nodes can be used for different domain groups.
tools.usage: Physics > Transport of Diluted Species in Porous Media > Species Source

parameters.name: S_i
parameters.description: Source term per species (mol/(m^3*s)).

tools.example:
1. Add Species Source on the contaminated zone.
2. Enter S_c = q_leak*c_leak for the leaking species.
3. Solve a transient study for plume evolution.
tools.notes: Available when Mass transport in porous media is enabled.

tools.name: Packed Bed (Transport of Diluted Species in Packed Beds)
tools.description: Main domain node of the packed-bed interfaces, modelling a bed of porous catalytic or reactant pellets with bimodal porosity. Bulk-fluid transport between pellets and intraparticle transport and reaction are solved simultaneously, with pellets represented in an extra dimension at each point. The node requires a Porous Material; multiple Pellets subnodes represent different pellet types.
tools.usage: Physics > Transport of Diluted Species in Packed Beds > Packed Bed (pb1); Java type: "PackedBed"

parameters.name: BedReactorType
parameters.description: PackedBed or moving packed bed.

parameters.name: poro
parameters.description: Bed (interparticle) porosity.

parameters.name: umb
parameters.description: Bed velocity for moving beds.

parameters.name: couplingCond
parameters.description: Pellet-fluid coupling (Flux or continuous concentration).

tools.notes: Extra-dimension meshing is controlled on the Pellets node; results inside pellets are evaluated with the pellet dataset.

tools.name: Pellets (Packed Bed)
tools.description: Subnode of Packed Bed defining intraparticle diffusion and reactions. Pellet types are Porous catalyst (diffusion and reaction inside the pellet, optional surface species) and Shrinking Core model (solid reactant core consumed by surface reactions). Pellet porosity, density, molar mass and size distribution are given here or inherited from the Porous Material.
tools.usage: Physics > Transport of Diluted Species in Packed Beds > Packed Bed > Pellets (pts1); Java type: "PorousPellet"

parameters.name: PelletType
parameters.description: Catalyst or Shrinking Core.

parameters.name: poro_pe
parameters.description: Pellet (intraparticle) porosity.

parameters.name: rho_pe, M
parameters.description: Pellet density and molar mass of the solid.

parameters.name: SurfaceSpecies / SolidSpecies
parameters.description: Species solved on pellet surfaces or in the core.

parameters.name: psizedist
parameters.description: Pellet size distribution option.

tools.notes: In Transport of Concentrated Species, a Pellet Temperature section and intraparticle flow are available.

tools.name: Pellet-Fluid Interface (Packed Bed)
tools.description: Subnode defining how pellet internals couple to the surrounding bed fluid. Continuous concentration assumes all mass-transfer resistance is inside the pellet (pore concentration at the surface equals the bulk value); Film resistance (mass flux) adds an external film coefficient computed from a Sherwood correlation such as Frossling or given directly.
tools.usage: Physics > Packed Bed > Pellet-Fluid Interface (pfi1); Java type: "PorousPelletFluidInterface"

parameters.name: couplingCond
parameters.description: Continuous concentration or Flux (film resistance).

parameters.name: ShModelList
parameters.description: Sherwood correlation, e.g. frosslingF, or user-defined Sh/hD.

parameters.name: hD
parameters.description: User mass transfer coefficient per species.

tools.notes: Only one coupling type should be used in a bed; additional nodes can target specific pellet types.

tools.name: Shrinking Core Reactions (Pellets)
tools.description: Subnode that defines reactions on the surface of a shrinking solid pellet core. The core shrinking rate follows from the consumption rate of the solid species (weighted by mass for several solids), and bulk species can be produced or consumed at the core surface. Rates can be user-defined or taken from a Chemistry interface with Define variables for porous pellets. Porous Layer Reactions handles reactions in the product layer.
tools.usage: Physics > Packed Bed > Pellets (Shrinking Core) > Shrinking Core Reactions (sreac1); Java type: "ShrinkingCoreReactions"

parameters.name: Rssurf / UserDefined
parameters.description: Core species surface reaction rate (mol/(m^2*s)).

parameters.name: Rs_<c>
parameters.description: Reaction rates of bulk species at the core surface.

parameters.name: PelletQ
parameters.description: Heat source from the core reactions.

tools.notes: Requires Pellet Type = Shrinking Core model on the Pellets node.

tools.name: Bed Inlet / Bed Outlet / Bed Wall (Moving Packed Bed)
tools.description: Boundary conditions for moving packed beds. Bed Inlet sets the pore concentrations of pellets entering the reactor (from bed fluid conditions, from pellet initial values or user-defined) and, for shrinking-core pellets, the initial core radius factor; Bed Outlet lets pellets leave; Bed Wall assumes no penetration and no viscous effects at walls. Inlet and outlet are normally placed on opposite boundaries.
tools.usage: Physics > Transport of Diluted Species in Moving Packed Beds > Bed Inlet (bin1) / Bed Outlet (bout1) / Bed Wall (wall1); Java types: "BedInlet", "BedOutlet", "Wall"

parameters.name: InitType
parameters.description: FluidPorousMedium (from bed fluid), from pellet initial values, or user defined inletcpe_<c>.

parameters.name: rc0f
parameters.description: Initial value factor for the core radius (shrinking core).

tools.notes: Boundaries must belong to pellet domains defined in the Porous Material.

tools.name: Porous Catalyst (Transport of Diluted Species in Porous Catalysts)
tools.description: Domain node for fluids moving through a catalytic porous medium, covering transfer to the surface, adsorption, surface reactions and desorption with a linear driving force model and lumped mass transfer coefficient. Fluid and Porous Matrix subnodes define phase properties; Adsorption and Surface Reaction subnodes add the surface processes, and surface species with site densities can be solved for.
tools.usage: Physics > Transport of Diluted Species in Porous Catalysts > Porous Catalyst (cat1); Java type: "PorousCatalyst"

parameters.name: Sarea
parameters.description: Specific surface area of the catalyst (m^2/m^3 or per mass).

parameters.name: SurfaceSpecies / initialValues
parameters.description: Surface species solved for and their initial surface concentrations.

parameters.name: gamman0
parameters.description: Site density per surface species.

parameters.name: enableAdsorption
parameters.description: Activate adsorption of bulk species.

tools.notes: The temperature model input is used for adsorption isotherms and surface rates.

tools.name: Surface Reaction (Porous Catalyst)
tools.description: Subnode of Porous Catalyst that supplies surface reaction source terms for bulk species, adsorbed species and surface species inside the catalyst. Rates are in mol/(m^2*s) per catalyst surface area and can be picked from a Chemistry interface defining surface reactions or entered as expressions.
tools.usage: Physics > Porous Catalyst > Surface Reaction (srcc1); Java type: "SurfaceReactionCatalyst"

parameters.name: Rsurf_<c>
parameters.description: Surface reaction rate for bulk species.

parameters.name: Rsads_<c>
parameters.description: Rate for adsorbed species.

parameters.name: Rssurf
parameters.description: Rates for surface species (e.g. comp1.chem.R_H_surf).

tools.notes: Several Surface Reaction subnodes can be used for different domain groups.

tools.name: Fracture (Transport of Diluted Species)
tools.description: Boundary node in the porous-media transport interfaces for mass transport along thin fractures where tangential transport dominates. Default Fluid (Fracture) and Fracture Material subnodes set convection, diffusion and fracture porosity, and the fracture thickness is a parameter so the fracture is not meshed as a domain. Attributes such as adsorption and reactions are the same as in the Fractures interface.
tools.usage: Physics > Transport of Diluted Species in Porous Media > Fracture (boundary) with Fluid (Fracture) and Fracture Material subnodes

parameters.name: dfr
parameters.description: Fracture thickness.

parameters.name: Fracture Material: epsilon_p
parameters.description: Fracture porosity.

parameters.name: Fluid (Fracture)
parameters.description: Velocity along the fracture and diffusivity.

tools.example:
1. Model a rock matrix with TDS in Porous Media.
2. Add Fracture on the internal fracture boundaries and set dfr = 1[mm].
3. Take the fracture velocity from Darcy's Law Fracture Flow and solve transiently.
tools.notes: Available only in some add-on products.

tools.name: Out-of-Plane Flux (Transport of Diluted Species)
tools.description: Domain node that adds fluxes through the out-of-plane faces of a reduced 1D or 2D model, turning them into volumetric sources. In 1D one out-of-plane flux per species is given; in 2D separate upside and downside fluxes can be set, for example as external convection with a mass transfer coefficient. Use it to reduce thin or slender geometries.
tools.usage: Physics > Transport of Diluted Species > Out-of-Plane Flux (1D and 2D components); in TCS Java type: "OutOfPlaneFlux"

parameters.name: J0,z / J0,u, J0,d
parameters.description: Out-of-plane molar flux (1D) or upside/downside fluxes (2D).

parameters.name: Flux type
parameters.description: General inward flux or external convection.

tools.example:
Application Library: Chemical_Reaction_Engineering_Module/Tutorials/thin_domain (Out-of-Plane Flux in Transport of Concentrated Species).
model.component("comp1").physics("tcs").create("opf1", "OutOfPlaneFlux", 2);
tools.notes: The 2D thickness or 1D cross-sectional area set on the interface is used to scale the source.

tools.name: Reaction Sources (Transport of Concentrated Species)
tools.description: Domain node that adds mass source terms (kg/(m^3*s)) from homogeneous or heterogeneous reactions to the mass-fraction equations. Sources are taken automatically from a coupled Chemistry interface or entered per species. The Mass transport to other phases option accounts for mass leaving or entering the fluid (condensation, deposition) so that the species from the mass constraint can also receive a source.
tools.usage: Physics > Transport of Concentrated Species > Reaction Sources (reac1); Java type: "ReactionSources"

parameters.name: Chemistry / chemTag
parameters.description: Coupled Chemistry interface or User defined.

parameters.name: R_<w>
parameters.description: Mass source per species.

parameters.name: MassTransferToOtherPhases
parameters.description: Allow net mass change of the fluid phase.

parameters.name: ReactingVolumeType
parameters.description: TotalVolume or PoreVolume in porous media.

tools.notes: With a Reacting Flow coupling the net mass source is also passed to the flow continuity equation.

tools.name: Mass Fraction (Transport of Concentrated Species)
tools.description: Boundary condition that fixes species mass fractions on exterior or interior boundaries. All species except the one computed from the mass constraint are specified. The Account for Stefan velocity option updates the Stefan velocity in a Reacting Flow coupling so that surface reactions or phase change at the boundary are consistently represented.
tools.usage: Physics > Transport of Concentrated Species > Mass Fraction (mf1); Java type: "MassFraction"

parameters.name: species / wbnd
parameters.description: Checkbox and mass fraction value per species.

parameters.name: uStefanActive
parameters.description: Account for Stefan velocity.

tools.notes: Inflow is preferred at inlets with convection because it can use a Danckwerts-type formulation.

tools.name: Vapor-Liquid Interface (Transport of Concentrated Species in Vapor)
tools.description: Exterior boundary feature for evaporation or condensation, prescribing the vapor pressure from liquid composition, temperature and pressure (for single liquids or mixtures). Concentration gradients driven by the vapor pressure produce species transfer, and the resulting mass flow and latent heat are made available to flow and heat transfer interfaces. The Vapor-Liquid-Solution Interface variant handles interior boundaries with a modelled liquid domain.
tools.usage: Physics > Transport of Concentrated Species in Vapor > Vapor-Liquid Interface (vl1); Java type: "VaporLiquidInterface"

parameters.name: VaporMassFraction / pressureModel
parameters.description: VaporPressure with Thermodynamics or user-defined vapor pressure.

parameters.name: LiquidPhaseConcentrationType
parameters.description: Liquid composition as mass, mole or volume fraction.

parameters.name: uStefanActive
parameters.description: Account for Stefan velocity.

parameters.name: EnableTransientInitialization
parameters.description: Ramp the interface condition at start-up.

tools.notes: Apply latent heat with a Boundary Heat Source; to move the interface use a Fluid-Fluid Interface in the CFD Module.
